about: Z3 verdict-line fixtures for the Z3 lane's reader (bench/statespace/lanes/z3.py) and the tab's (W1-T14): each captured case is the pinned engine's whole output, verbatim, with the verdict lines, verdict and reason the grammar gives, and the constants that the model printed after sat defines (expect.model: sorted names, [] for an empty model, null when no model is printed; the model is the last block after sat that is a list of define-fun items, with the declare-fun and forall items of a sort's universe); the synthetic cases are the grammar's edges. Written by scripts/spikes/W1-T29/capture-z3-lines.py, which records the execution as RUN-z3-verdict-lines; the expectations are stated there by hand, not computed by the lane.

cases.input:
(set-option :rlimit 0)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (> x 0))
(assert (> y 0))
(assert (> z 0))
(assert (= (+ (* x x x) (* y y y)) (* z z z)))
(check-sat)
(get-info :reason-unknown)
cases.note: the script's (set-option :rlimit 0) replaces the rlimit=5000000 of the command line, which stops the same query with unknown (canceled) in cli-unknown-rlimit: Z3 gave no answer within the capture's 3 s limit and was stopped; check_script refuses any script that sets :rlimit, :timeout or a memory limit

cases.input:
(declare-const sat Bool)
(simplify sat)
(check-sat-assuming (nonexistent))
cases.note: (simplify sat) prints the constant's name, sat, and the question then fails, so the grammar reads an answer that no question gave; check_script refuses simplify, eval and display before the question

cases.input:
(declare-const x Int)
(assert (> x 0))
(echo "unsat")
(exit)
)
cases.note: the script asks no question: Z3 runs (echo "unsat") and (exit) before it would read the stray ), and exits 0 with one line that reads as unsat; check_script refuses a script it cannot read, since Z3 runs every command before a fault

cases.input:
#| a | b |#
(echo "unsat")
| (check-sat)
cases.output:
unsat
(error "line 4 column 1: unexpected end of quoted symbol")

verdictLines: (error "line 4 column 1: unexpected end of quoted symbol")

cases.note: Z3 ends the #| block comment at the first |#, runs (echo "unsat"), and reads | (check-sat) as a quoted symbol that never ends, so no question is asked and the grammar reads unsat; a reader that takes each | for a quoted symbol sees one (check-sat) and no echo, so check_script refuses #| block comments

cases.note: SMT-LIB allows no backslash in a |quoted symbol|: Z3 reports an error and reads on from the backslash, where a reader that ends the symbol at the next | would not; check_script refuses such a script

cases.input:
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(declare-const amount Int)
(define-fun MAX_TRANSFER () Int 0)
(assert (! (> amount 0) :named amount-pos))
(assert (! (<= amount MAX_TRANSFER) :named under-max))
(check-sat)
(get-unsat-core)
cases.note: the named premises amount > 0 and amount <= MAX_TRANSFER contradict each other when MAX_TRANSFER = 0, so a claim guarded by them holds vacuously; the unsat core names both

cases.input:
p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
(check-sat)
cases.note: the command line reads the file as SMT-LIB: p is not a command, so Z3 reports an error, skips to the (check-sat) and answers sat about no assertions; Solver.from_string reads a text that starts 'p c' as DIMACS and answered unsat to the same clauses (values.from_string_dimacs_reading); check_script refuses a form outside any command

cases.input:
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(declare-const amount Int)
(define-fun MAX_TRANSFER () Int 0)
(assert (> amount 0))
(check-sat-assuming ((! (<= amount MAX_TRANSFER) :named under-max)))
(get-unsat-core)
cases.note: the command line assumes the named formula amount <= MAX_TRANSFER, which contradicts amount > 0 when MAX_TRANSFER = 0, and the unsat core it prints is that formula with MAX_TRANSFER replaced by 0; parse_smt2_string, which reads the api entry's assumptions, returns the named assumption as an implication from its name, which the name's being false satisfies, and the same question was sat read that way (values.parse_smt2_string_assumption_reading); check_script refuses an annotation in the question, so the lane runs neither entry on this one

cases.input:
(declare-const p Bool)
(assert (not p))
(check-sat-assuming ((|!| p :named q)))
cases.note: Z3 reads the quoted symbol |!| as the keyword !, so the question assumes p, which contradicts the assertion (not p), and Z3 reports no error; check_script removes the bars of a quoted symbol before it looks for an annotation, so it refuses this question too

cases.input:
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(declare-const amount Int)
(define-fun MAX_TRANSFER () Int 0)
(assert (> amount 0))
(declare-const under-max Bool)
(assert (=> under-max (<= amount MAX_TRANSFER)))
(check-sat-assuming (under-max))
(get-unsat-core)
cases.note: what check_script suggests instead of a named assumption: the Boolean constant under-max, assumed, which an assertion ties to amount <= MAX_TRANSFER; the premises contradict each other, so the question is unsat, and the unsat core names the constant
